identity.title: POCUS lung: absent lung sliding (+/- lung point, absent B-lines) for pneumothorax

technique.how: Supine patient; linear (or curvilinear/phased) probe longitudinal at the most anterior (non-dependent) intercostal spaces, 2nd-4th ICS midclavicular, both sides. Identify the pleural line between rib shadows and look for shimmering sliding and B-lines in B-mode; confirm with M-mode ('seashore' = sliding, 'barcode/stratosphere' = absent). Slide laterally to find a lung point.
technique.prerequisites: Depth 4-6 cm, focus at pleural line; hold probe still and observe several respiratory cycles.
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay decompression of a tension pneumothorax in extremis.

interpretation.positive_finding: Absent sliding with absent B-lines (A-lines only) is consistent with pneumothorax; a lung point (sliding alternating with no sliding at one location) is specific and defines its edge.
interpretation.negative_finding: Visible lung sliding or B-lines at the scanned point exclude pneumothorax at that point (pooled sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.98 vs CT/chest tube).
interpretation.pitfalls: Absent sliding also occurs with mainstem intubation, apnea, pleurodesis/adhesions, severe emphysema, ARDS and bullae; lung pulse (cardiac oscillation of pleural line) indicates no pneumothorax. Subcutaneous emphysema obscures the pleura; loculated or posterior air is missed.
interpretation.changes_what: Absent sliding + lung point in unstable patient: treat as pneumothorax and decompress. Sliding present: pneumothorax at that site excluded; look elsewhere for the cause of dyspnea.

estimates.population: Adults clinically suspected of pneumothorax (trauma and non-trauma); 8 studies, 1,048 patients
estimates.reference_standard: CT scan or release of air on chest tube placement
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.909/(1-0.982); LR- = (1-0.909)/0.982 from pooled sens 90.9%, spec 98.2% (Alrajhi 2012 abstract); CIs not computed
estimates.quote: Ultrasonography was 90.9% sensitive (95% CI, 86.5-93.9) and 98.2% specific (95% CI, 97.0-99.0) for the detection of pneumothorax.

estimates.target_condition: Pneumothorax as cause of acute respiratory failure (A' profile: anterior absent lung sliding + A lines + lung point)
estimates.population: 260 ICU patients with acute respiratory failure and definite diagnosis; pneumothorax n=9; operator: intensivist expert
estimates.quote: Anterior absent lung sliding plus A lines plus lung point indicated pneumothorax (n=9) with 81% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

estimates.population: Trauma patients undergoing eFAST; 75 studies, 24,350 patients (all components); operators mostly emergency physicians
estimates.reference_standard: CT, chest radiograph or chest tube (varies by study)
estimates.quote: Pooled sensitivities and specificities were calculated for the detection of pneumothorax (69% and 99% respectively)

sources.citation: Alrajhi K, Woo MY, Vaillancourt C. Test characteristics of ultrasonography for the detection of pneumothorax: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Chest. 2012;141(3):703-708.
Lichtenstein DA, Meziere GA. Relevance of lung ultrasound in the diagnosis of acute respiratory failure: the BLUE protocol. Chest. 2008;134(1):117-125.
Netherton S, Milenkovic V, Taylor M, Davis PJ. Diagnostic accuracy of eFAST in the trauma patient: a systematic review and meta-analysis. CJEM. 2019;21(6):727-738.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Not reliable after pleurodesis, in extensive subcutaneous emphysema, or when only the anterior chest is scanned in a supine patient with suspected posterior/loculated air.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Absent sliding with hypotension, distended neck veins or high airway pressures: decompress now; do not wait for CT.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Included studies were heterogeneous in operator (radiologists to emergency physicians) and probe; eFAST pooled sensitivity (0.69) is lower than dedicated lung-ultrasound studies (0.91), consistent with operator/protocol dependence.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Operator has completed basic lung POCUS training (identification of pleural line, sliding, B-lines, lung point, M-mode) and scans both hemithoraces at the non-dependent point.

extraction_notes: Pooled sens/spec quoted from Alrajhi 2012 abstract (full text not OA); LRs computed from those point estimates and flagged computed=true. BLUE protocol prevalence computed as 9/260. eFAST meta-analysis (Netherton 2019) added as a separate trauma-population estimate because sensitivity differs materially (0.69 vs 0.91). CIs for BLUE and eFAST are not given in abstracts and are left null. Newer meta-analyses appeared in search but were not fetched within budget.
